action.question: When should the per-thread `claude -p` analysis run? (It's spawned per stuck thread — real cost/latency, so caching matters.)

questions.question: When should the per-thread `claude -p` analysis run? (It's spawned per stuck thread — real cost/latency, so caching matters.)

options.label: Auto on load, cached
options.description: Opening/refreshing the UI auto-analyzes every stuck thread; results are cached so the same thread isn't re-analyzed until you force a re-run. Matches 'see the analysis up front.' Recommended.

options.label: Explicit button
options.description: Table shows all stuck threads + reasons on load; you click 'Analyze' per row (or 'Analyze all') to spend the claude -p calls. Most cost-control.

options.label: Background loop fills it
options.description: Run `manager --loop` to analyze continuously in the background; the UI just displays whatever analyses the loop has produced. No on-demand spawning from the UI.

questions.question: What should the investigator report for each stuck thread?

options.label: Recommendation + reasoning
options.description: A one-line recommended action (e.g. 'pick: No, skip migration' / 'looks done -> /close-work' / 'fork+resume+archive') plus 2-4 lines of why. Shown in the table, you accept/flag it.

options.label: Recommendation only
options.description: Just the one-line recommended action per thread, no reasoning text. Most compact table.

options.label: Full investigator output
options.description: Show the investigator's complete stdout per thread (verbose, most detail).
